subject: Fully specified geom still requires aes?

messages.author: 3a775dfa0a96bf95
messages.subject: Fully specified geom still requires aes?
parts:
I'm not sure I understand something very basic in ggplot.

Each geom's parameters can be either mapped to a variable or set
directly. But it seems that ggplot requires a mapping even if the
parameters are fully specified by setting and the parameters are
ignored. Why is that?

For example:

df <- data.frame(
Domain = factor(rev(c("Health","Self-Esteem","Goals &
Values","Money","Work","Play")),ordered=TRUE),
Satisfaction = c( -4, -6, 4, -3, -2, -2 ) )

This gives an error (No data to plot):

ggplot(df) +
geom_rect(xmin=-6.5,xmax=-3 ,ymin=-100,ymax=100,fill=gray(.3)) +
geom_point(data=df,aes(x=Satisfaction,y=Domain),size=5,shape=15)

even though every parameter needed to plot the rect is given.

But this works:

ggplot(df) +
geom_rect(aes(x=Satisfaction,y=Domain),xmin=-6.5,xmax=-3
,ymin=-100,ymax=100,fill=gray(.3)) + # add aes
geom_point(data=df,aes(x=Satisfaction,y=Domain),size=5,shape=15)

even though the values of x and y defined in the aes are ignored.

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: Fully specified geom still requires aes?
parts:
On Sat, May 9, 2009 at 5:17 PM, Stavros Macrakis <macr...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> I'm not sure I understand something very basic in ggplot.
>
> Each geom's parameters can be either mapped to a variable or set
> directly.  But it seems that ggplot requires a mapping even if the
> parameters are fully specified by setting and the parameters are
> ignored. Why is that?

This is one of the reasons why coming up with good error messages in
ggplot2 is so hard. This is perfectly valid plot specification (if a
little unusual) but because I tried to come up with an informative
error message when you didn't specify any data, I broke this case.
(The true situation is a little bit more complicated, iirc, because
some of the manipulations performed to the data when faceting require
a data frame, but this is essentially a implementation problem)

You might want to have a look at the annotate function that wraps up
this common pattern in a way that will work reliably. Your example
would become:

+ annotate("rect", xmin=-6.5,xmax=-3 ,ymin=-100,ymax=100,fill=gray(.3))

This is slightly shorter, and hopefully reflects the intent of that
line (to add an annotation) more clearly. If you look at the source
code of annotate you'll see it works by creating a data frame for the
position aesthetics - these are the only aesthetics that are
guaranteed to be present for every geom.

Regards,

Hadley

This one confused me too. My interest was adding text/rectangles etc
to plots
that consist of information not in the original data frame i.e. one-
off additions. The annotate
function seems like the way to go with this - is that right? In other
words, there is no need
to think about mapping back to a data frame in the way that the geoms
do.

I don't think the example actually works -

ggplot(df) +
geom_point(data=df,aes(x=Satisfaction,y=Domain),size=5,shape=15) +

Error in is.vector(X) : element 1 is empty;
the part of the args list of 'list' being evaluated was:
(x = x, xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, y = y, ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax)

David
